iteration_consistency_audit.why: the stored ladder mixes two iteration budgets: geometry_study solves its cheaper rungs at RUNG_ITERATION_FRACTION 0.6 of the production budget (180 iterations, floor 120) while the production rung runs the full 300. On a case still drifting at 300 that inconsistency enters the fit as if it were grid error.
iteration_consistency_audit.what_changed: the coarse and medium meshes were rebuilt from the production case with only the snappyHexMesh levels stepped down to each rung's own recorded setting (feature 4 / surface (3 4) / region 2 and feature 5 / surface (4 5) / region 3), then solved to 300 iterations instead of 180. Nothing else moved: same case, same background blockMesh (20 8 8), same kOmegaSST, same freestream, serial.
iteration_consistency_audit.reproduction_check: both rebuilt meshes reproduce their stored cell counts exactly (14,714 and 66,302) and their stored Cd exactly at the 180-iteration window (0.4709343 and 0.4213963), so the rebuild is the same measurement, not a new one

refit.reason_after: the observed order p = 7.082 falls outside the credible range 0.5 to 2.5

the_real_obstacle.statement: the production rung is still drifting at 300 iterations by more than the entire grid increment the observed order is fitted to. Coarse and medium are settled at 300 (final-window 2-sigma 2.41e-04 each, halves-drift below 4e-04); production is not (2-sigma 1.21e-03, halves-drift 1.75e-03). A FOURTH RUNG CANNOT FIX THIS. A finer rung makes the finest increment smaller, driving the signal further beneath the noise, not above it. The prerequisite is iterative convergence on the production mesh.

iteration_consistency_audit.levels_not_rewritten: levels[] is left exactly as published. The refit changes neither the conclusive flag nor the reportable band (both remain False and None), so there is nothing here that would improve a published number, and silently restating a live ladder is not this audit's call to make.
